clue.text: Sounded like a pig out of the pound — happy!

indicators.note: the pig's noise sits out of, that is outside, the abbreviation for the pound

parts.note: a pig makes a low snorting noise, so it grunted
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A pig escapes its pen and grunts contentedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pound' looks like an animal pen, but it is the currency, L, which goes inside GRUNTED. GRUNTLED is a jokey back-formation from 'disgruntled'.
explanation.definitionFit: The humorous back-formation from disgruntled means pleased or contented.

clue.text: Produce variety of green tea

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of green tea are rearranged

explanation.surface: Offering a range of green teas.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring into being or produce.

clue.text: Does it produce the gamine look. Arab style?

definitions.text: Does it produce the gamine look

parts.note: a street Arab is an old term for a homeless child, an urchin
a cut is a style of haircut or tailoring

explanation.surface: Asking whether an Arab fashion creates an elfin appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is the dated phrase 'street Arab', a ragged child. An urchin cut is a short cropped hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cropped, boyish haircut gives a woman an elfin gamine appearance.

clue.text: A letter from the Army

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A message has arrived from the military.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Executed charming picture

indicators.note: executed suggests beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: fetching means attractive or charming

explanation.surface: An attractive painting has been carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' looks like 'carried out' but means beheaded: FETCHING loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from an acid-bitten metal plate, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Responsibility for assault

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being to blame for an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in your care is your charge, and a charge is also a headlong rush or attack.

clue.text: Hastily top trees beginning to tilt

parts.note: the head is the top of something
firs are coniferous trees

indicators.note: the beginning of the word tilt supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: Treetops start to lean over.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in headlong, rashly and without thought, is going in hastily.

clue.text: Race broadcast

explanation.surface: A race is shown on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team race run in stages, and to relay is to transmit or pass on a signal.

clue.text: Last to finish on the river

parts.note: the end is the finish
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Coming in at the back of a boat race on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or persist, which is what enduring means.

clue.text: Sea-front fish smell

indicators.note: the front of the word sea gives its first letter

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A seaside fishy odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a powerful, unpleasant odour.

clue.text: Hot in attractive place that suits one

indicators.note: the letter for hot is placed in the word for attractive

parts.note: nice means pleasant or attractive
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warm, appealing spot that is just right for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's niche is the role or position they are best fitted for.

clue.text: Jazzman announced but is whistled at

parts.note: cat is slang for a jazz musician
called means proclaimed or announced aloud

explanation.surface: A jazz musician is introduced on stage, only to be jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: To catcall is to jeer or whistle derisively at someone, so the past form fits 'whistled at'.

clue.text: Defeat for an island people, followers of rugger

indicators.note: the island and the people come after the rugger abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union, which is rugger
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: An island nation of rugby fans suffers a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination means utter ruin or destruction, a crushing defeat.

clue.text: Entrance hall for the old to sit in

indicators.note: the old word is set to sit inside the word for, given as written

parts.note: taken as written
ye is an archaic form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A lobby where elderly people can sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' looks like elderly people, but it is the mock-archaic spelling of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is the lobby or vestibule just inside a theatre or hotel entrance.

clue.text: Marking the mattress cover

explanation.surface: Something marks the fabric on a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticking off items is marking them, and ticking is also the stout striped cotton used to cover mattresses.

clue.text: Severe Pope, though popular at first

indicators.note: the word for popular is placed first, before the papal name

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Clement is the name of fourteen popes

explanation.surface: A strict pontiff who was well liked when he started.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is harsh, rough and stormy.

clue.text: Recluse wins the lady's hand, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the letters are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: her means the lady's, and mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A loner gains a woman's hand in marriage, so rumour says.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit is someone who lives alone, apart from society.

clue.text: Game played on a diamond in North America?

definitions.text: Game played on a diamond in North America?

parts.words: Game played on a diamond in North America?
parts.note: a diamond suggests the baseball field, but here it is a gem's hard glittering stuff, slang for the frozen surface of a rink

explanation.surface: Describing baseball, played on a diamond across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' suggests baseball, but ice is slang for diamonds, and this sport is played on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the team sport played with sticks and a puck on a frozen rink, hugely popular in Canada and the US.

clue.text: The number on each pound is very delicate

parts.note: read as num-ber, something that numbs: ether is an anaesthetic
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: The figure for every pound is extremely fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that makes you numb: ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means airy, light and exquisitely fine.

clue.text: Hacks back to firm plaster

indicators.note: the word for hacks is read backwards

parts.note: to hack is to cut, so hacks means cuts
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Something is chopped back until the plaster is solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal, turning the word for hacks round before the abbreviation for company follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used for coating walls and for mouldings.

clue.text: Crooked bosses' haunt

indicators.note: crooked means bent or twisted, so the letters of bosses are rearranged

explanation.surface: Corrupt managers' hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haunt' looks like a noun, a hangout, but it is the verb: to preoccupy.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought that haunts you preoccupies your mind, as an obsession does.

clue.text: Long-suffering, but glaring about one

indicators.note: the word for glaring goes about, around, the numeral one

parts.note: patent means obvious or glaring
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stays tolerant while staring angrily at a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glaring' suggests staring, but here it means obvious: PATENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient person endures hardship or delay without complaint.

clue.text: Play on words — one without punch in this language

indicators.note: one sits without, outside, the word for punch

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
a jab is a quick punch
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wordplay joke lacks impact in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but means outside: I follows JAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is the tongue spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Red Indian becoming blue in the river

indicators.note: the rearranged colour goes in the name of the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the letters of blue change

explanation.surface: A Native American grows sad by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges the colour's letters to EBL; the Po is the river they sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pueblo are Native American peoples of the south-west US, named for their adobe villages; 'Red Indian' is the dated term.

clue.text: Country has sea change by order

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: the word sea is to undergo a change, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation alters its coastline by decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges the letters of sea; 'has' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was a Russian imperial edict, hence any arbitrary decree.

clue.text: Continue to play the historian

explanation.surface: Keeping up the performance as a scholar of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on is to carry on performing, and Lord Acton was a renowned Victorian historian.

clue.text: Attack by paper causes collapse

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a stroke is a sudden attack of illness, such as apoplexy

explanation.surface: A newspaper's assault brings about someone's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British daily tabloid. 'by' places it beside STROKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunstroke is a collapse caused by too much exposure to the sun's heat.

clue.text: Follow the scent

explanation.surface: Tracking an odour.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to track them, and a trail is the scent a hound follows.

clue.text: Short article on animal in the dogs' home

indicators.note: in an across answer the short article comes on, after, the animal

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal
terse means short or curt
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A brief piece about a creature living in an animal shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTERSEA Dogs' Home is a famous London animal rescue centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is the London district whose name is shorthand for its celebrated rescue shelter for stray dogs.

clue.text: Joint bank lending disclosure

indicators.note: the clue's words disclose, reveal, the letters sitting within bank lending

explanation.surface: A shared bank account's loans are made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a shared bank account, but it is the definition: a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint linking foot and leg.

clue.text: Baroque art one displaced

indicators.note: displaced means moved out of place, so the letters of art one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of baroque artwork has been moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque style is heavily ornamented and elaborate.

clue.text: Do a silly version that's not true

indicators.note: a version is a new form, so the letters of do a silly are recast

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a daft performance that is unfaithful to the original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'version' rearranges DOASILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disloyal is unfaithful, the opposite of true to a cause or friend.
